traditions.name: Alma Mater Statue
traditions.description: Lorado Taft's 1929 bronze of a robed woman with outstretched arms stands by Altgeld Hall to welcome students. Stop for a photo with her, a classic Illinois picture.

traditions.name: Altgeld Chimes
traditions.description: The chime of 15 bells in Altgeld Hall's tower has rung since 1920, marking the hours and playing short concerts. Listen near the tower for "Hail to the Orange," played at every concert.

traditions.name: Morrow Plots
traditions.description: Planted in 1876, these small fields are the oldest agricultural experiment fields in the United States and a National Historic Landmark. Walk past them beside the Undergraduate Library.

details.airportInfo: Willard Airport, in Savoy just south of campus, has daily flights to Chicago O'Hare and Dallas/Fort Worth. Many visitors fly into Chicago instead.
details.funFact: Architect Charles A. Platt designed the Main Library, one of several Georgian Revival buildings he designed for the campus.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are orange and blue, and the teams are the Fighting Illini.
details.transportationFact: The Champaign-Urbana Mass Transit District runs frequent buses across campus, and students ride with their i-card.

buildings.name: Altgeld Hall
buildings.description: Built in 1896–97 as the University Library, this Richardsonian Romanesque hall was designed by Nathan Ricker and James M. White of the university's architecture department. Its bell tower holds the University Chime, which marks the hours.
buildings.architect: Nathan Ricker and James M. White

buildings.name: Foellinger Auditorium
buildings.description: Clarence H. Blackall's Beaux-Arts auditorium closes the south end of the Main Quad. The round hall, 120 feet across, is crowned by a copper dome and is the university's largest lecture hall.

buildings.name: Main Library
buildings.description: Charles A. Platt designed this Georgian Revival library, begun in 1924 to replace Altgeld Hall when the collections outgrew it. It holds the University Archives and the Rare Book and Manuscript Library.

buildings.name: Smith Memorial Hall
buildings.description: Built in 1917–20 just east of Foellinger Auditorium, this Beaux-Arts music hall was the first building on campus paid for entirely by a private gift. Captain Thomas J. Smith dedicated it to his wife, Tina Weedon Smith.
buildings.architect: James M. White and George E. Wright

buildings.wiki: Krannert Center for the Performing Arts
buildings.name: Krannert Center for the Performing Arts
buildings.description: Illinois alumnus Max Abramovitz designed this performing arts complex, which opened in 1969 with four indoor venues seating about 4,000 in all. Its main lobby is floored with teak from Thailand.

traditions.name: Rose Well House
traditions.description: Campus legend says a kiss under the Rose Well House at midnight brings lasting romance. The little pavilion near Dunn Woods is also a favorite spot for proposals.

traditions.name: Sample Gates
traditions.description: The limestone Sample Gates mark the entrance to the Old Crescent from Kirkwood Avenue. Walk through them and take a photo, as many new graduates do.

traditions.name: Herman B Wells Statue
traditions.description: A bronze of the beloved former president sits on a bench with his hand held out. Shake it: the story goes that a student whose family shakes his hand will graduate on time.

traditions.name: Showalter Fountain
traditions.description: The fountain in the Fine Arts Plaza shows the birth of Venus surrounded by bronze fish. Count the fish and look for the one that replaced a fish taken after the 1987 basketball title.

details.airportInfo: Indianapolis International, north of Bloomington, is the nearest airport with airline service.
details.funFact: Many of the campus buildings are built of Indiana limestone, the local stone the state is known for.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are cream and crimson, and the teams are the Hoosiers.
details.transportationFact: IU Campus Bus routes loop around the campus, and Bloomington Transit buses connect it with the rest of the city.

buildings.name: Indiana Memorial Union
buildings.description: Granger and Bollenbacher designed this Collegiate Gothic student union, dedicated in 1932. At nearly 500,000 square feet it is one of the largest student unions in the world and includes a hotel.

buildings.name: Lilly Library
buildings.description: Eggers & Higgins designed this limestone rare book and manuscript library, dedicated in 1960 on the Fine Arts Plaza. It began with the collection of Josiah K. Lilly Jr. and now holds millions of manuscripts.
buildings.address: Fine Arts Plaza, Indiana University, Bloomington, IN 47405

buildings.name: Eskenazi Museum of Art
buildings.description: I. M. Pei and Partners designed the museum's building, completed in 1982 as a play on sharp angles. It was renovated and reopened in 2019 and holds about 45,000 objects.

buildings.wiki: Mies Building for the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design
buildings.name: Mies Building
buildings.description: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe drew these plans in 1952 for a fraternity house that was never built. Rediscovered in 2013, they were finally built for the art and design school, with glass walls and white steel like his Farnsworth House.

buildings.name: Wylie House
buildings.description: Built in 1835, this brick house was the home of Andrew Wylie, the first president of Indiana University. Its blend of Georgian and Federal styles was old-fashioned for its time, and the university runs it as a house museum.

traditions.name: Old Capitol Photo
traditions.description: Graduates like to pose in front of the Old Capitol, by its columns and the doorway with "Iowa" above it. Take your own photo on the steps at the heart of the Pentacrest.

traditions.name: Kinnick Wave
traditions.description: At home football games, after the first quarter the whole crowd turns and waves to the patients watching from the children's hospital above the east stands. If you go to a game, join in.

details.airportInfo: The Eastern Iowa Airport, near Cedar Rapids to the north of Iowa City, is the nearest airport with airline service.
details.funFact: The Greek Revival Old Capitol, Iowa's first state capitol building, stands at the center of the Pentacrest, ringed by four Beaux-Arts halls.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are black and gold, and the teams are the Hawkeyes.
details.transportationFact: The university's free Cambus service runs routes across campus and to the hospitals.

buildings.name: Old Capitol
buildings.description: John F. Rague designed this Greek Revival building, begun in 1842 as the main government building of the state of Iowa. It is now the central landmark of the campus and a National Historic Landmark.
buildings.address: Pentacrest, University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA 52242

buildings.wiki: University of Iowa Museum of Natural History
buildings.name: Macbride Hall
buildings.description: Proudfoot & Bird designed this Beaux-Arts hall, completed in 1908 as the Natural Sciences Building on the Pentacrest. It houses the university's Museum of Natural History.
buildings.address: 17 N Clinton St, Iowa City, IA 52242

buildings.wiki: University of Iowa Stanley Museum of Art
buildings.name: Stanley Museum of Art
buildings.description: BNIM Iowa, led by Rod Kruse, designed this brick museum, opened in 2022 to replace the building lost to the 2008 flood. It sits above the flood plain and holds Jackson Pollock's Mural.
buildings.address: Gibson Square, University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA 52242

buildings.name: Voxman Music Building
buildings.description: LMN Architects and Neumann Monson designed this six-story music school, opened in October 2016. It replaced the original Voxman building on the Iowa River, destroyed in the 2008 flood.
buildings.address: 93 E Burlington St, Iowa City, IA 52242
buildings.newUse: School of Music and Concert Hall

traditions.name: Rub Testudo's Nose
traditions.description: Students rub the nose of the bronze terrapin Testudo outside McKeldin Library for luck, and leave small offerings during finals. Give his nose a rub as you pass.

details.airportInfo: Reagan National, across the Potomac in Arlington, Virginia, is the closest major airport. BWI and Dulles also serve the region.
details.funFact: Morrill Hall, finished in 1898, was the only academic building left untouched by the Great Fire of 1912 that swept the campus.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are red, white, black and gold, and the teams are the Terrapins.
details.transportationFact: The university's Shuttle-UM buses serve campus and nearby neighborhoods, and the College Park–University of Maryland Metro station links to Washington.

buildings.name: Memorial Chapel
buildings.description: Henry Powell Hopkins designed this Georgian chapel, completed in 1952 to honor members of the university who died in military service. Its steeple is the highest point on campus.

buildings.name: Rossborough Inn
buildings.description: Finished in 1803, this Federal-style inn on the old Washington and Baltimore Turnpike is the oldest building on campus, older than the university itself. Its lower wings were added in 1938.
buildings.address: Baltimore Ave, University of Maryland, College Park, MD 20742

buildings.name: Morrill Hall
buildings.description: Built in 1898 as Science Hall in the Second Empire style, this is the oldest academic building on campus still in use. It was renamed for Senator Justin Morrill, author of the Land-Grant Colleges Act.
buildings.address: Morrill Quad, University of Maryland, College Park, MD 20742

buildings.name: Iribe Center
buildings.description: A team from HDR led by Brian Kowalchuk designed this computer science building, completed in 2019 at a cost of $152 million. It holds research floors and a large auditorium.
buildings.address: 8125 Paint Branch Dr, College Park, MD 20742

buildings.name: Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center
buildings.description: Moore Ruble Yudell designed this 318,000-square-foot arts center as an "academic village" of courtyards and halls, opened in 2001 with six performance venues. It was the largest single building ever built by the State of Maryland.
buildings.address: University of Maryland, College Park, MD 20742

traditions.name: The Rock
traditions.description: Given by the Class of 1873, the Rock beside the Red Cedar River is painted over again and again with new messages. Stop to see what it says today.

traditions.name: The Spartan Statue
traditions.description: The nearly 10-foot bronze Spartan is a favorite photo backdrop, especially at graduation. Take a selfie with it.

traditions.name: Beaumont Tower Open Tower
traditions.description: Beaumont Tower opens to visitors on the first Wednesday of each month and at graduation. Go up to see the carillon and the view over campus.

traditions.name: MSU Dairy Store
traditions.description: The MSU Dairy Store was voted Grand Champion in the American Dairy Science Association's 2025 Ice Cream Competition. Stop at its Anthony Hall shop and try a flavor.

traditions.name: W. J. Beal Botanical Garden
traditions.description: Professor William J. Beal began this garden in 1873, and it is claimed to be the oldest continuously maintained university botanical garden in the US. Stroll it for free any day during daylight hours.

traditions.name: MSU Horticulture Gardens
traditions.description: The gardens on Bogue Street hold more than 700 rose cultivars and the Michigan 4-H Children's Garden. Wander them for free any day.

traditions.name: Red Cedar River Trail
traditions.description: A trail runs across campus along the south bank of the Red Cedar River, and the Lansing River Trail starts here. Bike or walk it, or kayak the river.

traditions.name: The Izzone
traditions.description: Named for coach Tom Izzo, the Izzone is the student section of about 5,000 at men's basketball games in the Breslin Center. Catch a game to hear it roar.

traditions.name: Magic Johnson Statue
traditions.description: A 12-foot bronze of Earvin "Magic" Johnson, who led MSU to the 1979 national title, has stood outside the Breslin Center since 2003. Snap a photo with it.

traditions.name: Spartan Marching Band March
traditions.description: On football Saturdays the band warms up on Adams Field, then marches past the Spartan Statue and up Red Cedar Road to the stadium about an hour before kickoff. Line the route to cheer it on.

details.airportInfo: Capital Region International Airport in Lansing is the nearest airport with airline service.
details.funFact: Beaumont Tower stands on the site of College Hall, the first building in America erected for teaching scientific agriculture.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are green and white, and the teams are the Spartans.
details.transportationFact: CATA buses run routes through campus and connect it with East Lansing and Lansing.

buildings.name: Beaumont Tower
buildings.description: Donaldson and Meier designed this Collegiate Gothic tower, completed in 1928 on the site of College Hall, the first building on campus. It was given by alumnus John W. Beaumont as a monument to teaching.
buildings.address: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.wiki: Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum
buildings.name: Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum
buildings.description: Zaha Hadid designed this contemporary art museum, opened in 2012. Its steel and concrete frame is wrapped in pleated stainless steel and glass.
buildings.address: 547 E Circle Dr, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Cowles House
buildings.description: Built in 1857 to house faculty, this is the oldest surviving building on campus, though only its foundation and two outer walls are original. It has been the official president's residence since 1941.
buildings.address: W Circle Dr, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: MSU Union
buildings.description: Chicago firm Pond and Pond designed this Collegiate Gothic student union, built from 1923 to 1925. It has arched openings, gables and tall windows.
buildings.address: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Linton Hall
buildings.description: Detroit firm Marsh & Arnold designed this Romanesque library and museum of limestone and fieldstone, completed in 1881 under architect William P. Appleyard. It held the president's office until 1968 and now houses the College of Arts and Letters.
buildings.address: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Eustace–Cole Hall
buildings.description: Built in 1888 to ideas from horticulturist Liberty Hyde Bailey, this was the first separate horticulture laboratory in the United States. It mixes Queen Anne, Richardsonian Romanesque and Shingle Style features and is the only main-campus building on the National Register of Historic Places.
buildings.architect: Liberty Hyde Bailey; William P. Appleyard
buildings.address: 468 E Circle Dr, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Cook–Seevers Hall
buildings.description: Professor Samuel Johnson designed this building, opened in 1889 as the college's first agricultural laboratory. It is named for entomologist Albert J. Cook and, since a 2018 renovation, for alumnus Gary L. Seevers.
buildings.address: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Chittenden Hall
buildings.description: George Lohman designed this first campus building made for dairy work, dedicated in 1901; doors high in its north wall once let the cows in. It later housed Forestry, whose name is carved over the entrance, and became home to the Graduate School in 2014.
buildings.address: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Marshall–Adams Hall
buildings.description: College architect Edwyn A. Bowd designed this 1902 laboratory, the first freestanding bacteriology laboratory in the United States. Its red brick walls and fieldstone-arched Richardsonian Romanesque entry now house the Department of Economics.
buildings.address: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Justin S. Morrill Hall of Agriculture
buildings.description: College architect Edwyn A. Bowd designed this five-story neoclassical hall, the largest building on campus when it was dedicated in 1909. Renamed in 2013 for Senator Justin Morrill, author of the land-grant act, it still houses the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources.
buildings.address: 446 W Circle Dr, East Lansing, MI 48824
buildings.newUse: College of Agriculture and Natural Resources

buildings.name: MSU Museum
buildings.description: Edwyn Bowd designed this building as the college library, completed in 1924, and it became the museum's home after the new Main Library opened in 1955. The museum, founded in 1857, was Michigan's first Smithsonian Affiliate.
buildings.address: 409 W Circle Dr, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Spartan Stadium
buildings.description: Edwyn Bowd designed the first 14,000-seat stadium, opened in 1923; its sides were double-decked in 1957, the year it was named Spartan Stadium. A 2005 west-side addition of suites and a press box made it the tallest building in East Lansing.

buildings.name: Demonstration Hall
buildings.description: Bowd–Munson designed this Romanesque Revival hall, built in 1928 with offices, classrooms and a riding arena for military science. Once home to Spartan basketball and hockey, it now serves ROTC and the Spartan Marching Band.
buildings.address: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Jenison Fieldhouse
buildings.description: Opened in 1940 and named for alumnus Frederick Cowles Jenison, this three-story late Art Deco fieldhouse has reliefs of baseball, basketball and football players above its three main doors. Magic Johnson's 1979 national champions played here, and a plaque outside recalls the 1963 "Game of Change."
buildings.address: Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Breslin Student Events Center
buildings.description: HNTB and Giffels, Hoyem, Basso designed this arena, opened in 1989 and named for alumnus and administrator Jack Breslin. Home of Spartan basketball, it gained the Tom Izzo Basketball Hall of History in a 2016–2017 renovation.

buildings.name: Munn Ice Arena
buildings.description: Grand Rapids firm Daverman Associates designed this hockey-only arena, opened in 1974 and named for coach and athletic director Clarence "Biggie" Munn. Its rink was named for longtime coach Ron Mason in 2023.

buildings.name: Abrams Planetarium
buildings.description: Ralph Calder Associates of Detroit designed this planetarium, opened in 1963 and named for aerial photography pioneer Talbert Abrams and his wife Leota. Its 150-seat sky theater sits under a fifty-foot dome.

buildings.name: Facility for Rare Isotope Beams
buildings.description: SmithGroup JJR designed this U.S. Department of Energy user facility for nuclear science, completed in 2022. Scientists use it to make and study rare isotopes, short-lived atomic nuclei not normally found on Earth.
buildings.address: 640 S Shaw Ln, East Lansing, MI 48824

buildings.name: Main Library
buildings.description: Completed in 1955 on the north bank of the Red Cedar River, overlooking Beal Botanical Garden, this research library replaced the old one, which became the MSU Museum, and students lined up to pass the books across. An east wing added in 1967 tripled its shelf space, and it holds one of the world's largest comic art collections and the Vincent Voice Library.
buildings.address: 366 W Circle Dr, East Lansing, MI 48824

traditions.name: Goldy Gopher Statue
traditions.description: A bronze Goldy Gopher stands beside a granite M outside Coffman Memorial Union, a gathering spot and a symbol of school spirit. Stop by for a photo.

details.airportInfo: MSP is south of the Twin Cities. From campus, take the Green Line light rail downtown and change to the Blue Line.
details.funFact: Frank Gehry's stainless steel Weisman Art Museum, finished in 1993, sits on the bluff above the Mississippi River.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are maroon and gold, and the teams are the Golden Gophers.
details.transportationFact: The free Campus Connector bus links the East Bank, West Bank and St. Paul campuses, and the Metro Green Line light rail runs through campus.

buildings.name: Northrop Auditorium
buildings.description: Clarence H. Johnston designed this Classical Revival auditorium, built in 1928–29 at the north end of Northrop Mall. It was rebuilt inside by HGA and reopened in 2014.

buildings.name: Weisman Art Museum
buildings.description: Frank Gehry designed this museum of folded stainless steel, completed in 1993 on the bank of the Mississippi. Gehry also designed its 2011 addition.

buildings.name: Walter Library
buildings.description: State Architect Clarence H. Johnston designed this Beaux-Arts library, built between 1922 and 1924 on Northrop Mall. It now houses the science and engineering library.

buildings.name: Coffman Memorial Union
buildings.description: Opened in 1940 at the south end of Northrop Mall, this seven-story student union has a stripped classical exterior and Streamline Moderne interiors.

traditions.name: Archie the Mammoth
traditions.description: Students rub the foot of Archie, the bronze mammoth outside Morrill Hall, for luck before tests and projects. Give his foot a rub or a high-five.

details.nickname: There Is No Place Like Nebraska
details.airportInfo: Lincoln Airport, northwest of downtown, is the nearest airport. Omaha's Eppley Airfield has more flights.
details.funFact: Philip Johnson's Sheldon Museum of Art, opened in 1963, is built of Italian travertine around a grand hall and central staircase.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are scarlet and cream, and the teams are the Cornhuskers.
details.transportationFact: StarTran buses link City, East and Innovation campuses, and students get a bus pass through their transit fee.

buildings.name: Sheldon Museum of Art
buildings.description: Philip Johnson designed this modern museum of Italian travertine, opened in 1963. Its grand hall and central staircase lead to collections of American art.

buildings.name: Architecture Hall
buildings.description: Mendelssohn, Fisher and Lawrie designed this Richardsonian Romanesque library, built in 1895. It is the oldest building on campus and now houses the College of Architecture.

buildings.name: Mueller Tower
buildings.description: This stone carillon tower, built in 1949, was named for alumnus and donor Ralph S. Mueller. A restoration begun in 2025 scanned and catalogued each of its 1,700 stones.
buildings.address: City Campus, University of Nebraska–Lincoln, Lincoln, NE 68588

buildings.name: Memorial Stadium
buildings.description: Opened in 1923, the stadium honors Nebraskans who served in the nation's wars. Its architects, John Latenser Sr. and Ellery L. Davis, worked without pay.
buildings.architect: John Latenser Sr. and Ellery L. Davis

traditions.name: The Rock
traditions.description: Students have painted the Rock since the 1940s, often guarding it for a day before painting it overnight. Stop by to see the latest message.

traditions.name: Weber Arch
traditions.description: New students march in through Weber Arch at the start of their time at Northwestern, and seniors march out through it near the end. Walk through the arch from Sheridan Road onto campus.

traditions.name: Shakespeare Garden
traditions.description: This quiet garden on the north side of campus is one of the stops on the admissions campus tour map. Visit it on a walk through campus.

details.airportInfo: O'Hare, west of Evanston, is the region's main airport. Chicago Midway also serves the city.
details.funFact: University Hall, finished in 1869, is the oldest original building on campus, and its old clockworks are now at the Smithsonian.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are purple and white, and the teams are the Wildcats.
details.transportationFact: CTA Purple Line and Metra trains stop near campus, and the university's Intercampus shuttle links Evanston with the Chicago campus.

buildings.name: University Hall
buildings.description: Gurdon P. Randall designed this Victorian Gothic hall, begun in 1868 and finished in 1869. It is the oldest original building on campus and now houses the English department.

buildings.name: Deering Library
buildings.description: James Gamble Rogers designed this Collegiate Gothic library, which opened in 1933 and served as the main library until 1970. It houses the University Archives and the Music Library.

buildings.name: Pick-Staiger Concert Hall
buildings.description: Edward D. Dart designed this concert hall of precast concrete and glass, completed in 1975. All 1,003 seats have a clear view of the stage.

buildings.name: Dearborn Observatory
buildings.description: Cobb and Frost designed this limestone observatory in the Richardsonian Romanesque style, built in 1888–89. It was moved in 1939 to make room for the Technological Institute.

traditions.name: The Long Walk
traditions.description: The Long Walk crosses the Oval toward University Hall; first-year students were once forbidden to use it. Walk its length across the heart of campus.

traditions.name: Buckeye Grove
traditions.description: A buckeye tree is planted beside Ohio Stadium for each of Ohio State's first-team All-Americans, each with a plaque. Look for the names of famous players among the trees.

traditions.name: Victory Bell
traditions.description: The Victory Bell in Ohio Stadium's southeast tower is rung after every Ohio State win. Listen for it after a home game.

details.airportInfo: John Glenn Columbus International, east of downtown Columbus, is the main airport for the region.
details.funFact: Ohio Stadium's horseshoe has an upper deck that hangs over the lower one, and its north rotunda was modeled on the dome of the Pantheon in Rome.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are scarlet and gray, and the teams are the Buckeyes.
details.transportationFact: The free Campus Area Bus Service runs routes around campus, and COTA buses serve the rest of Columbus.

buildings.name: Thompson Library
buildings.description: Boston firm Allen & Collens designed the main library in the Italian Renaissance Revival style, completed in 1912 on the Oval. A 2009 renovation restored its original east front.
buildings.address: The Oval, Ohio State University, Columbus, OH 43210

buildings.name: Ohio Stadium
buildings.description: Howard Dwight Smith designed this horseshoe-shaped stadium, opened in 1922 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Its north rotunda was modeled on the dome of the Pantheon in Rome.

buildings.name: Wexner Center for the Arts
buildings.description: Peter Eisenman and Richard Trott designed this arts center, opened in 1989. Its white metal grid suggests scaffolding, and the building follows two street grids that differ by 12.25 degrees.

buildings.name: University Hall
buildings.description: The first University Hall, a High Victorian Gothic design by Jacob Snyder from 1873, was torn down in 1971. The present building, completed in 1976, copies the original's architecture.

buildings.name: Knowlton Hall
buildings.description: Mack Scogin Merrill Elam designed this home for the architecture school, completed in 2004. Its post-tensioned concrete frame is wrapped in shingles of white Georgia marble.

traditions.name: Nittany Lion Shrine
traditions.description: Heinz Warneke's limestone lion, dedicated in 1942, is the most photographed spot on campus. Many students take a photo here on their first day and again before graduation.

traditions.name: Berkey Creamery
traditions.description: The university's creamery, whose ice cream short course dates back to 1892, sells its own ice cream in the Food Science Building. Stop in for a cone.

details.airportInfo: State College Regional Airport, called University Park Airport until 2023, is the nearest airport.
details.funFact: Charles Klauder designed both Rec Hall, which opened in 1929, and the rebuilt Old Main, finished in 1930.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are blue and white, and the teams are the Nittany Lions.
details.transportationFact: CATA runs the fare-free Blue Loop, White Loop and Red Link on campus, and community routes to the rest of State College.

buildings.name: Old Main
buildings.description: The first Main Building was completed in 1863. Charles Klauder's Federal Revival rebuilding, with its clock tower, was finished in 1930 and holds the president's office.

buildings.name: Rec Hall
buildings.description: Charles Klauder, who also designed the Palestra in Philadelphia, chose a Georgian design for this field house, opened in 1929. The gymnastics, volleyball and wrestling teams still compete here.

buildings.name: Palmer Museum of Art
buildings.description: Allied Works designed the museum's new home in the Arboretum, opened in 2024. Its linked pavilions are clad in regional sandstone with perforated stainless steel sunscreens.

buildings.name: Eisenhower Auditorium
buildings.description: Built from 1971 to 1973 to a plan by consultants Sanders & Bicksler and Bolt Beranek and Newman, this Brutalist-inspired hall opened in 1974. It was first named University Auditorium.

traditions.name: Bell Tower Kiss
traditions.description: Legend says a couple who kiss under the Bell Tower and then walk past the nearby Stone Lion Fountain will one day marry. Visit the tower at the center of campus.

traditions.name: Hello Walk
traditions.description: The Hello Walk began as the path to University Hall and now covers the walks across Memorial Mall. Smile and say hello to everyone you pass.

details.airportInfo: Indianapolis International, southeast of West Lafayette, is the nearest major airport.
details.funFact: The Purdue Bell Tower, finished in 1995, carries the bells of the old Heavilon Hall tower, which came down in 1956.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are old gold and black, and the teams are the Boilermakers.
details.transportationFact: Free Purdue Campus Transit loops circle the campus, and CityBus routes connect West Lafayette with Lafayette.

buildings.name: Purdue Bell Tower
buildings.description: This 160-foot brick tower, a gift of the class of 1948, was completed in 1995 at the heart of campus. It is a modern take on the old Heavilon Hall tower and has a clock on each face.

buildings.name: Elliott Hall of Music
buildings.description: Walter Scholer designed this 6,005-seat theater, completed in 1940, with J. André Fouilhoux, one of the architects of Radio City Music Hall, as consultant. It is one of the largest proscenium theaters in the world.

buildings.name: Purdue Memorial Union
buildings.description: Chicago firm Pond and Pond designed this student union, opened in 1924 as a memorial to Purdue students who fought in World War I. It holds restaurants, lounges, a bowling alley and a hotel.
buildings.address: 101 N Grant St, West Lafayette, IN 47907

buildings.name: Engineering Fountain
buildings.description: Sculptor Robert Youngman designed this 38-foot water sculpture of 228 tons of concrete, a gift of the class of 1939. It was dedicated in 1989.

traditions.name: Willie the Silent
traditions.description: The 1928 bronze of William the Silent, Prince of Orange, known to students as Willie the Silent, is one of the best-loved statues on campus. Find him on Voorhees Mall.

traditions.name: Old Queens Bell
traditions.description: The bell in the cupola of Old Queens rings for convocation, commencement and other great occasions, and inspired the song "The Bells Must Ring." Look up at the cupola from the Queens Campus.

details.airportInfo: Newark Liberty, northeast of New Brunswick, is reached by NJ Transit trains on the Northeast Corridor Line.
details.funFact: Old Queens, begun in 1809, was designed by John McComb Jr., who also designed New York City Hall.
details.languageInfo: The school color is scarlet, and the teams are the Scarlet Knights.
details.transportationFact: Free Rutgers buses link the College Avenue, Busch, Livingston and Cook/Douglass campuses, and NJ Transit trains stop at New Brunswick station.

buildings.name: Old Queens
buildings.description: John McComb Jr. designed this brownstone Federal building, begun in 1809 and finished in 1825. It is the oldest building at Rutgers and a National Historic Landmark.

buildings.name: Kirkpatrick Chapel
buildings.description: Henry Janeway Hardenbergh designed this Gothic Revival chapel early in his career, and it was completed in 1873. It is one of six buildings on the historic Queens Campus.
buildings.address: Queens Campus, Rutgers University, New Brunswick, NJ 08901

buildings.wiki: Geology Hall, New Brunswick, New Jersey
buildings.name: Geology Hall
buildings.description: Henry Janeway Hardenbergh designed this stone hall, built in 1871–72 to house science classes and the Rutgers Geology Museum. The museum now fills the whole building.
buildings.address: Queens Campus, Rutgers University, New Brunswick, NJ 08901

buildings.name: Winants Hall
buildings.description: Van Campen Taylor designed this hall, completed in 1890 as the first dormitory at Rutgers College. A renovation restored its Roman brick fireplaces and four-story oak staircase.

traditions.name: Abe Lincoln on Bascom Hill
traditions.description: The seated Abraham Lincoln statue in front of Bascom Hall is a highlight of commencement weekend photos. Take your picture beside him at the top of the hill.

traditions.name: Terrace Sunburst Chairs
traditions.description: The sunburst chairs on the Memorial Union Terrace are one of the university's best-known symbols. Sit in one by Lake Mendota.

traditions.name: Babcock Hall Ice Cream
traditions.description: Ice cream made by the university's dairy at Babcock Hall is a student staple and a visitor favorite. Try a scoop.

details.airportInfo: Dane County Regional Airport, northeast of downtown Madison, is the city's airport.
details.funFact: North Hall, built in 1851 to a design by John F. Rague, was the university's first building and still stands on Bascom Hill.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are cardinal and white, and the teams are the Badgers.
details.transportationFact: Madison Metro buses cross campus, and students ride with a university bus pass.

buildings.name: Science Hall
buildings.description: Henry C. Koch and Allan Conover designed this Romanesque hall, built in 1888 with sixteen corbelled brick chimneys. It is a National Historic Landmark.
buildings.architect: Henry C. Koch and Allan Conover

buildings.wiki: University of Wisconsin Armory and Gymnasium
buildings.name: Red Gym
buildings.description: Allan Conover and Lew F. Porter designed this Romanesque Revival armory and gymnasium, built in 1894. It looks like a red brick castle on the shore of Lake Mendota.
buildings.architect: Allan Conover and Lew F. Porter

buildings.name: Memorial Union
buildings.description: Arthur Peabody designed this Italian Renaissance Revival union, built in 1926–28 on Lake Mendota. Its Terrace by the water is a popular gathering place.

buildings.name: Washburn Observatory
buildings.description: David R. Jones designed this Italianate observatory, completed in 1881. It was a major research center for about 50 years, and its telescope is still used by students and the public.

buildings.name: North Hall
buildings.description: John F. Rague designed this Greek Revival hall, built in 1851 as the university's first building. It now houses the Department of Political Science.
buildings.address: Bascom Hill, University of Wisconsin–Madison, Madison, WI 53706

traditions.name: Yell-O Duck Statue
traditions.description: A 1,000-pound bronze of the Duck throwing the "O" stands between Matthew Knight Arena and the Ford Alumni Center. Throw the O beside it for a photo.

traditions.name: Bill Bowerman Statue
traditions.description: A 2000 bronze of coach and Nike co-founder Bill Bowerman stands at the corner of Hayward Field. Visit it on a walk around the track stadium.

details.airportInfo: Eugene Airport, northwest of the city, is the nearest airport.
details.funFact: Ellis F. Lawrence, dean of the university's architecture school, designed both the Knight Library and the art museum.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are green and yellow, and the teams are the Ducks.
details.transportationFact: Lane Transit District's EmX bus rapid transit stops along the edge of campus, and students ride LTD buses with their ID.

buildings.name: University Hall
buildings.description: W. W. Piper designed this Italianate hall, built from 1873 to 1876 as the university's first building. Known for most of its history as Deady Hall, it is a National Historic Landmark with Villard Hall.

buildings.name: Villard Hall
buildings.description: Completed in 1886, this Second Empire hall is the second-oldest building on campus. It was named for railroad magnate Henry Villard, the university's first benefactor.

buildings.name: Knight Library
buildings.description: Ellis F. Lawrence designed the main library, built in 1937, mixing Lombardic Romanesque and Art Deco. It holds more than 3 million volumes.

buildings.name: Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art
buildings.description: Ellis F. Lawrence designed this brick and cast stone museum, which opened in 1933 to house Gertrude Bass Warner's collection of Asian art. Its style mixes Romanesque and other influences.

buildings.name: Johnson Hall
buildings.description: State Architect William C. Knighton designed this American Renaissance hall, built in 1914–15. It is the main administration building of the university.

traditions.name: Tommy Trojan
traditions.description: The bronze Trojan warrior in Hahn Plaza is the campus's favorite meeting place. Before the UCLA game it is wrapped in duct tape and guarded around the clock by the Trojan Knights.

traditions.name: Hecuba Statue
traditions.description: The statue of Hecuba, queen of Troy, was unveiled in 2017 in the central plaza of USC Village as a counterpart to Tommy Trojan. Visit her in the plaza.

details.airportInfo: LAX, southwest of campus, is the main airport for Los Angeles.
details.funFact: Widney Alumni House, dedicated in 1880, is the oldest university building in Southern California.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are cardinal and gold, and the teams are the Trojans.
details.transportationFact: The Metro E Line has stations next to campus along Exposition Park, and USC runs its own campus shuttles.

buildings.name: Doheny Library
buildings.description: Ralph Adams Cram designed the exterior and Samuel Lunden the interiors of this 1932 library, built in a Northern Italian Romanesque style of rounded arches, pale brick and limestone.
buildings.architect: Ralph Adams Cram and Samuel Lunden
buildings.address: University Park Campus, Los Angeles, CA 90089

buildings.name: Widney Alumni House
buildings.description: Dedicated in 1880, this was the university's original building and is the oldest university building in Southern California. It is a California Historical Landmark.

buildings.name: Zumberge Hall of Science
buildings.description: John and Donald Parkinson designed this Romanesque Revival science hall, completed in 1928.
buildings.address: University Park Campus, Los Angeles, CA 90089

buildings.name: Leavey Library
buildings.description: Completed in 1994, this undergraduate library returned to the Romanesque Revival look of the older campus buildings. It is named for Thomas E. Leavey, founder of Farmers Insurance.
buildings.address: University Park Campus, Los Angeles, CA 90089

buildings.name: Wallis Annenberg Hall
buildings.description: Harley Ellis Devereaux designed this $150 million building for the Annenberg School, built of concrete and steel with brick veneer in the Collegiate Gothic style. It opened in 2014.
buildings.address: University Park Campus, Los Angeles, CA 90089
